name: OR-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+14 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Bentz holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.0M raised, $1.4M on hand vs. under $100K for Beck)
Prediction markets price Bentz at roughly 95% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
model.rationale: Eastern Oregon's R+14 lean, Bentz's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing his win odds near 95% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with only a modest Democratic environment providing any offset.
model.watch: Any emergence of polling showing Beck competitive, or significant outside spending on his behalf, would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Cliff Bentz seeks a third term representing a rural, R+14 district that Republicans have held for decades. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised about $1 million and holding $1.4 million on hand, while Democrat Chris Beck has raised under $100,000. No independent groups have reported spending in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets give Bentz roughly a 95% chance of winning. A favorable national environment for Democrats is the main factor working in Beck's favor, but it is unlikely to overcome the district's strong Republican lean and the incumbent's resource edge.
